cohort: The cohort consisted of 124 pregnant women with singleton cephalic pregnancies, gestational age after 37 weeks, Bishop scores below six, undergoing induction of labor, and no prior history of cesarean delivery or contraindications to vaginal delivery.
finding: Ultrasonographic evaluation of LUS and MLUS thickness before induction of labor is a promising parameter to predict cesarean delivery, with LUS thickness demonstrating better sensitivity and specificity.
mod_finding: Higher LUS and MLUS thickness values were significantly associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery after induction of labor.
